Below are two editions of DeepSeek's API pricing page: the English one, and the Chinese one.
They list the same models. The English page prints the price table in USD; the Chinese page
prints the same models' prices in CNY.

Report only what these pages print. Every number you report must be one that literally appears
on the page you took it from. Do not compute, round, convert, or supply a figure from memory.
If a number is not printed there, the run must fail rather than carry your guess.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else - no prose and no markdown fences:

{
  "schedule": {
    "quote":   the sentence that states which days the peak rule applies to, copied word for
               word from the page,
    "days":    the weekdays that sentence names, as three-letter abbreviations from
               ["Mon","Tue","Wed","Thu","Fri","Sat","Sun"],
    "windows": every peak window, as [["HH:MM","HH:MM"], ...], in UTC, in the order the page
               lists them
  },
  "models": [
    {
      "id":      the API model name - the leftmost value on the MODEL row,
      "version": the matching value on the MODEL VERSION row,
      "USD":     this model's prices, from the ENGLISH page,
      "CNY":     this model's prices, from the CHINESE page
    }
  ]
}

The price table has three row groups, in this order:

  1M INPUT TOKENS (CACHE HIT)   ->  "inputCacheHit"
  1M INPUT TOKENS (CACHE MISS)  ->  "inputCacheMiss"
  1M OUTPUT TOKENS              ->  "output"

Each row group has an OFF-PEAK row and a PEAK row. The table's columns are the models, in the
same order the MODEL row lists them. So each price set looks exactly like this, with a number
printed on the page in every leaf:

{"inputCacheHit": {"offPeak": 0, "peak": 0},
 "inputCacheMiss": {"offPeak": 0, "peak": 0},
 "output": {"offPeak": 0, "peak": 0}}

Report each figure as a bare number - the digits only. The page prints its prices with a
currency on them ("$0.003", "0.02元"); strip that and give the number. So the English page's
"$0.3" is `0.3` and the Chinese page's "9元" is `9`.

The sentence "Off-peak rates are half of the peak rates" states a rule, not a source of numbers:
report the off-peak figures the page prints, not ones derived from that sentence.
